summary: Laplace's equation on a rectangle: the steady temperature when one side is held at f and the other three at 0. The graph shows it as a heat map.

methods.name: Separation of variables
methods.reason: Three sides are held at 0, so product solutions can be superposed to match the fourth.

steps.title: Separate the variables
steps.text: Look for solutions that are a product of a function of each variable. Substituting and dividing by the product puts each variable on its own side, so both sides equal a constant, written \(-\lambda\).

steps.title: Solve the eigenvalue problem
steps.text: The boundary conditions apply to the spatial factor. The two sides facing each other in the \(x\) direction are both held at 0, so that direction gives the eigenvalue problem; its solutions are sines.

steps.title: Solve in the other direction
steps.text: The other factor satisfies \(Y'' - \lambda_n Y = 0\), whose solutions are hyperbolic. It must vanish on the side opposite the data, which selects

steps.title: Superpose
steps.text: Sum the products; three sides are then at 0 whatever the coefficients are.

steps.title: Find the coefficients
steps.text: On the side \(y = b\) the hyperbolic ratio is 1, so the series must equal \(f(x)\) there. The coefficients are the expansion coefficients of the data in the eigenfunctions, found with their orthogonality.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked numerically: the series satisfies the equation at sample points and the boundary conditions. With 20 terms it reproduces the boundary values closely.
